findings.claim: The acceptance file's generatedAt (23:50:41.807Z) precedes the recordedAt of the receipt embedded inside it (23:51:21.908Z) and the Playwright run it summarizes (startTime 23:51:01.355Z), so the provenance timestamp of the assembled record does not actually denote when the record was assembled.
findings.evidence: Hunk: `"generatedAt": "2026-08-29T23:50:41.807Z"` vs. embedded `"recordedAt": "2026-08-29T23:51:21.908Z"` in the same file, and `"startTime": "2026-08-29T23:51:01.355Z"` in task-11-playwright-report.json. Any consumer ordering or validating evidence by generatedAt will mis-sequence this artifact relative to the evidence it contains.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the field to reflect gate-start time (e.g. `gateStartedAt`) or stamp `generatedAt` when the acceptance record is finalized, after the embedded receipt and Playwright report exist.

findings.claim: The re-recorded run moved every performance metric in the negative direction — search p95 latency rose ~36% (14.3ms → 19.4ms), panel-open p95 rose (11.9ms → 13.2ms), and throughput fell below the nominal 500 events/sec emit rate (498.88) — yet status remains "pass" because the evidence schema carries no threshold fields, so the task-11 'responsive 500-event interaction' criterion has no enforced numeric guard and regressions pass silently.
findings.evidence: Hunk in task-11-browser-evidence.json: `"achievedEventsPerSecond": 498.8825031929222` (< 500 for `"emittedEvents": 5000`), `"searchLatencyP95Ms": 19.399999998509884` vs. prior 14.3; criterion task 11 requires proving 'responsive 500-event interaction' but the artifact contains only raw numbers with no assertion bounds.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit threshold fields (e.g. maxSearchLatencyP95Ms, minEventsPerSecond) to the evidence schema and have the gate assert against them, so 'responsive' is verified rather than implied by a passing status.
